id: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.chart-trace
title: 'Chart-trace + satisfiability verdict: no-leak forces closed chart traces;
  a connected divisor must sit in ONE chart'
projects:

summary: "LANDED 2026-07-25 (run 0048), kernel-checked warning-free by lake env lean,\
  \ both files in the\ndefault build.\n\nPicard/DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean (commit\
  \ 49866bdd1) — THE NECESSITY.\n * supportLocus_inter_chart0_eq_iUnion / _chart1_\
  \ : the chart trace IS the finite union of the\n   chart's piece traces (cover0/cover1\
  \ one way, Scheme.basicOpen_le the other).\n * isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart0_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty\
  \ (+ chart-1 twin), and the\n   assembler-shaped isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak:\
  \ the hnoLeak hypothesis of\n   isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning forces BOTH\
  \ chart traces closed in the relative curve.\n * not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart0\
  \ / _chart1 : contrapositive — a system whose chart trace\n   is not closed admits\
  \ NO adaptation satisfying the assembler's clause.\n\nPicard/DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean\
  \ (commit 206967379) — THE SUFFICIENCY.\n * subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus\
  \ : a piece missing the support has a UNIT equation,\n   so its colength module\
  \ vanishes (the colength companion of the landed overlap version).\n * supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint\
  \ and forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint :\n   swallow-or-miss gives the\
  \ assembler's hnoLeak with no fibre, tube or idempotent.\n * forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint\
  \ : clause (c1)-finite at every piece.\n * subset_chart0_or_disjoint_chart0 / _chart1_\
  \ : the dichotomy the shape imposes on the divisor.\n\nWHAT IT SETTLES. The lane's\
  \ obligation is chart-trace closedness, a property of the system and the\ntwo pinned\
  \ charts alone. Refining the cover cannot help (it adds constraints while the union\
  \ of the\ntraces is fixed), so leak-image route (b) is dead; and the tube/idempotent\
  \ machinery cannot\nmanufacture it, so leak-image route (a) is exactly chart-avoid.\
  \ The lane is therefore a chart-design\nproblem, not a fibre-analysis problem.\n\
  \nPicard/DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean (commit 40f357de8) — THE SATISFIABILITY VERDICT.\n\
  \ * subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak : leak-freeness makes the\
  \ piece trace CLOSED\n   and the piece is OPEN, so the trace is clopen in the support;\
  \ a preconnected support forces it\n   empty or total. Swallow-or-miss is therefore\
  \ not an extra hypothesis for a connected divisor —\n   it is what leak-freeness\
  \ already says.\n * supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected : IsPreconnected\
  \ supportLocus plus leak-freeness at\n   every piece implies supportLocus subset\
  \ V_0 OR supportLocus subset V_1. No nonemptiness needed.\n * not_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isPreconnected\
  \ : contrapositive — a connected divisor confined\n   to neither pinned chart admits\
  \ NO leak-free adaptation, over any base, after any shrink.\n\nSO: IsCertified is\
  \ satisfiable for a connected divisor only if the divisor avoids pi^{-1}(0) or\n\
  pi^{-1}(infinity). Seven rounds were spent proving hypotheses of an interface whose\
  \ satisfiability\nhad never been checked.\n\nPicard/DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean (commit\
  \ 5651710d6) — THE KEYSTONE, closing Ground's I-0334.\n * IsAffineOpen.isClosed_zeroLocus_inter_of_finite_quotient\
  \ — the converse of the abstract finiteness\n   engine: Module.Finite makes Spec(Gamma(V)/I)\
  \ -> Spec R finite hence universally closed; it factors\n   through X and X -> Spec\
  \ R is separated, so the first leg is universally closed\n   (UniversallyClosed.of_comp_of_isSeparated)\
  \ and its range — the trace — is closed.\n * supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength\
  \ / supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_finite_colength — clause (c1)\n   and leak-freeness\
  \ are the SAME condition at a piece. This is the equivalence I-0209 asserted and\n\
  \   nobody had proved.\n * supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified — the verdict\
  \ for IsCertified itself.\nAxioms of the keystone: exactly [propext, Classical.choice,\
  \ Quot.sound].\n"

########## AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.field-size.yaml
id: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.field-size
title: 'Field-size: over a small finite field, what is DivFamZar? — the one remaining
  human decision'
projects:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
summary: "ANSWERED 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 4). Not blocked any more, and not a\
  \ human decision after all —\nthe bound is a theorem, sharp in both directions.\
  \ Deliverable: informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 4\n§4.4 (commit d7e8348ce). Inbox\
  \ I-0346's standing question is discharged.\n\nTHE ANSWER.  R1 -- varying the pinned\
  \ pair of P^1-points per cover member, i.e. the p1-aut ->\nfibre-avoid -> cert-relocalize\
  \ chain -- is correct IF AND ONLY IF |P^1(k)| >= n + 2, where n is\nthe degree,\
  \ pinned to the genus g by the functor.\n\nBoth directions come from one fibrewise\
  \ reduction (ADDENDUM 4 §4.2).  For c in P^1(k) let W_c be\nthe image in Spec R\
  \ of supp D meeting pi^{-1}(c); it is closed because supp D is finite over R,\n\
  and s in W_c iff the FIBRE supp(D_s) meets pi^{-1}(c).  Since D_s is finite of degree\
  \ n over\nkappa(s), its image in |P^1| has at most n closed points.\n  IF: pick\
  \ c in P^1(k) outside that image and any c' /= c; then Spec R minus W_c confines\
  \ D to the\n  chart complementary to pi^{-1}(c).  Doing this at every s gives a\
  \ Zariski cover on which the\n  divisor is confined, with the pair varying per member\
  \ -- exactly what R1 allows.\n  ONLY IF: if the sum over c in P^1(k) of e_c is at\
  \ most n, where e_c is the minimal degree of a\n  closed point of C over c, then\
  \ a divisor of the form sum_c q_c + padding lies in W_c for EVERY\n  c in P^1(k),\
  \ and no pinned pair confines it.\n\nCONSEQUENCES, and they decide the certificate\
  \ route.\n * p1-aut is NOT dead.  It is correct over every infinite field, and over\
  \ F_q whenever q >= g+1.\n * It cannot discharge the challenge on its own.  Challenge.lean:96-99\
  \ states the Jacobian over an\n   ARBITRARY field and archon-protected.yaml forbids\
  \ adding a hypothesis, so R1 must be paired\n   with descent (dat-g) or replaced.\n\
  \ * Of the three options this leaf was opened to choose between, (a) \"accept |P^1(k)|\
  \ >= n+2 as a\n   hypothesis\" is now known to be exactly the right hypothesis and\
  \ exactly what the challenge\n   forbids; (b) descent from a big enough k' is viable\
  \ and is the pairing R1 needs; (c) degree-d\n   closed points is unnecessary --\
  \ it is subsumed by R2, which is cleaner.\n * R2 is the only field-uniform fix and\
  \ is no longer a gamble: supp D is finite over R, hence\n   contained in a single\
  \ affine open of C x_k Spec R (avoidance for families, Stacks 0B8B), so a\n   cover\
  \ with one straddling piece always exists.  Generalising FinCoverData's piece type\
  \ to\n   arbitrary affine opens of the relative curve is the statement the geometry\
  \ already supports.\n\nRelated and settled the same round: the on-stratum witness\
  \ the no-go lacked now exists at g >= 2\nover any field (ADDENDUM 4 §4.3), so the\
  \ no-go is not vacuous on the campaign's stratum; and\nADDENDUM 3's shrink-stability\
  \ argument was the wrong criterion (a span-top cover cannot delete a\npoint) --\
  \ under the criterion it stated, the campaign's own genus-0 example would be evaded.\n"
